description: Outcome & Expectation evaluations for diagnosing-tempo-ingestion-and-health covering discarded-span rate/size drops, Tempo 2.x ring health & gossip port 7946 WAL safety, Tempo 3.x Kafka partition lag & vParquet4 block-builders, multi-tenant X-Scope-OrgID rejections, OTel Collector exporter port/pipeline misconfigurations, trace time gaps, degraded TempoStack CRs, missing metrics-generator processors, regional backend connectivity vs metrics scrape failures, and 2-phase override remediation.

evals.prompt: After turning on `loadGeneratorFloodHomepage` in `flagd` (50 Locust users flooding `frontend-proxy:8090`), `otel-demo` microservices started losing spans in our primary Grafana Tempo cluster in `observability`. Run a full Tempo health and ingestion check for `otel-demo`, pinpoint why spans are being discarded, and preview a safe per-tenant override increase without applying it live yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://server/capabilities` and `tempo://deployment/overview`, calls `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="default", tenant="otel-demo")`, identifies `SPANS_DISCARDED` (`rate_limited` / `max_bytes_per_trace_exceeded` / `live_traces_exceeded` during the `loadGeneratorFloodHomepage` surge), reads `tempo://overrides/default/otel-demo` to capture the current `etag`, previews `tempo_patch_tenant_overrides(..., expected_etag=..., dry_run=True)` without calling `dry_run=False`, and asks operator confirmation.
expectations: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` on the primary Tempo backend covering health, rings, ingestion, config, and operator status
Identifies `SPANS_DISCARDED` drop reasons triggered during the `loadGeneratorFloodHomepage` surge
Reads `tempo://overrides/default/otel-demo` to capture `etag` and previews `tempo_patch_tenant_overrides(..., dry_run=True)`
Stops at the confirmation gate without invoking `dry_run=False`

evals.prompt: TraceQL searches for `checkout-service` and `product-catalog-service` intermittently return HTTP 500s on our Tempo 2.6 distributed cluster `tempo-2x-degraded-ring` in `observability`. Diagnose its component and hash-ring health, and explain how to handle stateful ingester pods safely so recent traces aren't lost.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://system/backends/tempo-2x-degraded-ring` (and/or `tempo://deployment/overview`) and calls `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="tempo-2x-degraded-ring")`, surfacing `RING_MEMBER_UNHEALTHY` (**Critical**) on the ingester ring and `RING_CHECK_FAILED` (**Warning**) on compactor/memberlist gossip port `7946` (plus `COMPONENT_NOT_RUNNING` if present), and warns to preserve stateful Tempo 2.x ingester WAL PVCs/flush before restarting pods.
expectations: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `tempo-2x-degraded-ring` (and inspects `tempo://system/backends/tempo-2x-degraded-ring` or `tempo://deployment/overview`)
Classifies `RING_MEMBER_UNHEALTHY` / `COMPONENT_NOT_RUNNING` as Critical and `RING_CHECK_FAILED` (memberlist gossip port `7946`) as Warning
Warns against force-deleting stateful Tempo 2.x ingester pods without preserving WAL volumes / flushing in-memory blocks

evals.prompt: On our Grafana Tempo 3.x distributed cluster `tempo-3x-distributed` in `observability` (tenant `otel-demo`), newly emitted `PlaceOrder` traces from `opentelemetry-otel-collector` take nearly 4 minutes to appear in search! Run Tempo diagnostics and explain which Tempo 3.x components are lagging and how to remediate it.
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="tempo-3x-distributed", tenant="otel-demo")` detecting `tempo_major_version: 3` (`architecture_generation: "3.x"`) and `PARTITION_LAG_OBSERVED` (`tempo_ingest_group_partition_lag_seconds`), explains the Tempo 3.x stateless `distributor -> ingest -> Kafka -> block-builder -> vParquet4 object storage` pipeline (distinct from `otel-demo`'s own `kafka:9092` broker and Tempo 2.x stateful ingesters), and recommends scaling Tempo `block-builder` consumers or object-storage upload concurrency.
expectations: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `tempo-3x-distributed` (tenant `otel-demo`) and surfaces `PARTITION_LAG_OBSERVED` (`tempo_ingest_group_partition_lag_seconds`)
Correctly describes the Tempo 3.x `distributor -> ingest -> Kafka -> block-builder -> vParquet4` architecture
Recommends scaling Tempo `block-builder` replicas / partition consumer throughput rather than Tempo 2.x stateful ingesters

evals.prompt:
After turning on multi-tenancy on `tempo-3x-distributed` in `observability`, `opentelemetry-otel-collector` in `otel-demo` started getting HTTP 400/401 rejections and zero traces show up in Tempo. Check diagnostics on `tempo-3x-distributed` and audit this Collector exporter configuration:
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo-distributor.observability.svc.cluster.local:4318
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="tempo-3x-distributed")` surfacing `TENANT_HEADER_REQUIRED` (**Critical**) and runs `scripts/check_otel_exporter_config.py` against the `opentelemetry-otel-collector` config, catching two defects: (1) `NO_TENANT_HEADER` — missing `headers.X-Scope-OrgID: otel-demo` required when `multitenancy_enabled: true`, and (2) `PORT_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` — gRPC `otlp/tempo` exporter pointing at HTTP port `:4318` instead of `:4317` (or switching exporter type to `otlphttp/tempo`).
expectations: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `tempo-3x-distributed` surfacing `TENANT_HEADER_REQUIRED`
Runs `check_otel_exporter_config.py` detecting `NO_TENANT_HEADER` (missing `X-Scope-OrgID: otel-demo`)
Detects `PORT_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` (`otlp` gRPC exporter targeting HTTP port `:4318` instead of `:4317`) and outputs corrected Collector YAML

evals.prompt:
We ran `helm upgrade product-catalog charts/product-catalog/ -n otel-demo --set otel.enabled=true` and Tempo in `observability` is healthy, yet traces from a newly deployed collector in `otel-staging` never arrive in Tempo. Check Tempo backend health and service attributes, and audit this `opentelemetry-otel-collector` configuration:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.observability.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
    headers:
      X-Scope-OrgID: otel-staging
  debug:
    verbosity: basic
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
```
evals.expected_output: Follows the zero-traces decision tree: verifies Tempo health via `tempo_get_diagnostics`, checks `tempo_get_attribute_values(attribute="resource.service.name", tenant="otel-staging")`, and runs `scripts/check_otel_exporter_config.py` against the Collector config—flagging `NOT_IN_TRACES_PIPELINE` because `otlp/tempo` is declared under `exporters:` but omitted from `service.pipelines.traces.exporters: [debug]`.
expectations: Verifies Tempo health and `resource.service.name` presence via `tempo_get_diagnostics` and `tempo_get_attribute_values`
Runs `check_otel_exporter_config.py` and identifies `NOT_IN_TRACES_PIPELINE` (`otlp/tempo` missing from `service.pipelines.traces.exporters`)
Provides the corrected `service.pipelines.traces.exporters: [otlp/tempo]` configuration

evals.prompt: `PlaceOrder` trace `9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d` in `otel-demo` took `4.8` seconds end-to-end from `frontend-proxy` through `checkout-service`, `shipping-service`, and `quote`, yet the spans visible in the Tempo waterfall only add up to `900ms`! Diagnose why `3.9` seconds of the trace is blank.
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_summarize_trace` and `tempo_get_trace` on `9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d` plus `tempo_get_diagnostics`, identifying `TRACE_TIME_GAPS` (`critical_path_duration_ms < 50%` of `total_duration_ms`) and checking whether child spans (`quote` PHP `:8080` or `flagd` `:8013` evaluations) had `otel.enabled=false` in their Helm chart, dropped W3C `traceparent` HTTP headers between Rust `shipping-service` and PHP `quote`, or hit `SPANS_DISCARDED` (`max_bytes_per_trace_exceeded`).
expectations: Calls `tempo_summarize_trace` / `tempo_get_trace` on `9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d` and `tempo_get_diagnostics`
Identifies `TRACE_TIME_GAPS` because critical-path span coverage is `< 50%` of the `4.8s` total trace duration
Checks `SPANS_DISCARDED` (`max_bytes_per_trace_exceeded`), `otel.enabled=false` on downstream `OTEL-APP` services (`quote`/`email`), and broken W3C `traceparent` propagation

evals.prompt: Our `TempoStack` custom resource `tempo-otel-degraded` in namespace `observability` became unhealthy right after an object-storage secret rotation (pointing at `tempo-otel-missing-s3-secret` instead of `tempo-otel-s3-credentials`). Inspect Tempo Operator status in `observability` without exposing secret values, diagnose what failed, and validate a fix via server-side dry-run without applying it live yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://operator/crs/observability` and `tempo://operator/manifests/TempoStack/observability/tempo-otel-degraded`, runs `tempo_get_diagnostics` surfacing `OPERATOR_CR_NOT_READY` (**Critical**), pinpoints `Ready=False` (`StorageSecretNotFound` / `tempo-otel-missing-s3-secret`) without reading raw Kubernetes Secret data, updates `spec.storage.secret.name` to `tempo-otel-s3-credentials`, and previews via `tempo_apply_operator_cr(..., dry_run=True)` without calling `dry_run=False`.
expectations: Reads `tempo://operator/crs/observability` and `tempo://operator/manifests/TempoStack/observability/tempo-otel-degraded` via MCP resources
Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` surfacing `OPERATOR_CR_NOT_READY` and identifies the `Ready=False` storage secret condition without dumping Secret values
Previews the corrected `TempoStack` manifest (`tempo-otel-s3-credentials`) via `tempo_apply_operator_cr(..., dry_run=True)` without calling `dry_run=False`

evals.prompt: Grafana Service Graphs (`frontend -> checkout-service -> payment/cart-service/product-catalog-service/shipping-service`) and TraceQL Metrics panels went completely blank on our `tempo-no-local-blocks` Tempo instance in `observability`, even though looking up individual traces by `trace_id` still works fine. Diagnose what is disabled on `tempo-no-local-blocks` and show how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="tempo-no-local-blocks")` and inspects `tempo://server/capabilities` / `tempo://system/backends/tempo-no-local-blocks`, identifying `METRICS_GENERATOR_PROCESSOR_ABSENT` (`service-graphs`, `span-metrics`, and `local-blocks` missing from `metrics_generator.processors`) and `OVERRIDES_API_DISABLED` (`user_configurable_overrides` disabled), and shows the exact `tempo.yaml` / `TempoStack` configuration to enable `["service-graphs", "span-metrics", "local-blocks"]`.
expectations: Calls `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `tempo-no-local-blocks` and checks `tempo://server/capabilities` / `tempo://system/backends/tempo-no-local-blocks`
Surfaces `METRICS_GENERATOR_PROCESSOR_ABSENT` (missing `service-graphs`, `span-metrics`, `local-blocks`) and `OVERRIDES_API_DISABLED`
Provides exact `metrics_generator.processors` (`service-graphs`, `span-metrics`, `local-blocks`) enablement guidance

evals.prompt: Check our two regional Tempo backends `otel-eu` and `otel-us` in `observability`—`otel-eu` is failing all trace queries completely, while `otel-us` serves TraceQL searches normally but isn't reporting any dropped-span counters. Inspect both backends, classify the severity difference, and give concrete Kubernetes troubleshooting steps for each.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://system/backends` and runs `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `otel-eu` and `otel-us`, classifying `BACKEND_UNREACHABLE` on `otel-eu` as **Critical** (Tempo `:3200` HTTP query endpoint down, DNS mismatch, TLS error, or NetworkPolicy block) and `INGESTION_METRICS_UNREACHABLE` on `otel-us` as **Info** (TraceQL search works, but `/metrics` cannot be scraped from the gateway URL so `SPANS_DISCARDED` / `PARTITION_LAG_OBSERVED` counters aren't visible), giving concrete K8s Service/NetworkPolicy/metrics-port steps for both.
expectations: Reads `tempo://system/backends` and runs `tempo_get_diagnostics` on `otel-eu` and `otel-us`
Distinguishes Critical `BACKEND_UNREACHABLE` on `otel-eu` from Info `INGESTION_METRICS_UNREACHABLE` on `otel-us`
Provides concrete Kubernetes Service DNS, port `:3200`, NetworkPolicy, and `/metrics` scrape remediation steps for both

evals.prompt: We confirmed that tenant `otel-demo` on our primary Tempo cluster in `observability` is hitting single-trace byte limits during `recommendationCacheFailure` and `loadGeneratorFloodHomepage` runs. Preview raising `max_bytes_per_trace` to `20971520` (20 MiB) safely with optimistic concurrency first, apply the change live as approved, and verify Tempo ingestion health afterward.
evals.expected_output: Reads `tempo://overrides/default/otel-demo` to obtain the current `etag`, calls `tempo_patch_tenant_overrides(backend_id="default", tenant="otel-demo", merge_patch={"max_bytes_per_trace": 20971520}, expected_etag=..., dry_run=True)` to inspect the unified diff, executes `tempo_patch_tenant_overrides(..., dry_run=False, confirm=True)`, and re-runs `tempo_get_diagnostics(backend_id="default", tenant="otel-demo")` to verify post-change health.
expectations: Reads `tempo://overrides/default/otel-demo` first to fetch the current `etag`
Calls `tempo_patch_tenant_overrides` chronologically with `dry_run=True` first, followed by `dry_run=False, confirm=True`
Re-runs `tempo_get_diagnostics` for `otel-demo` afterward to verify post-change health
